N PHOTOS | The Philippine Air Force (PAF) on Thursday carried out back-to-back humanitarian missions to assist disaster-affected communities in Batanes and Cagayan, delivering food aid and transporting stranded individuals to safety.

A PAF C-130 cargo aircraft flew to Basco, Batanes, to deliver 1,000 family food packs and bring home 88 stranded individuals — including tourists and locally stranded persons — to Pasay City. The mission was executed with support from the Philippine National Police, Bureau of Fire Protection, 30th Marine Company, Marine Battalion Landing Team 10, and both PAF and Army reservists.

On the same day, two Black Hawk helicopters transported more than 800 boxes of relief goods from Laoag City to Calayan Island, Cagayan, for residents affected by Super Typhoon Nando. The supplies, provided by the Department of Social Welfare and Development and the Department of Education, were flown in by pilots and crew of the 205th Tactical Helicopter Wing with assistance from Tactical Operations Group 1. Rex Espiritu

📷 PAF 

For more news updates, visit https://t.co/rmQCnNSOvI.
